questions.question: An aircraft weighs mg = 25,000 N and has the drag polar CD = 0.020 + 0.045 CL2. What is its minimum thrust required in steady level flight?
questions.explanation: Minimum thrust required is TR,min = 2mg√(K CD,0) = 2 × 25,000 × √(0.045 × 0.020) = 50,000 × 0.030 = 1,500 N. 750 N drops the factor of 2 (giving only the parasite drag part); 3,000 N doubles the answer; 1,125 N multiplies by K instead of 2√(K CD,0).

questions.question: At the minimum-thrust speed VTR,min in steady level flight, how do the parasite drag and the induced drag compare?
options: They are equal, so CD = 2 CD,0
Induced drag is three times parasite drag, so CD = 4 CD,0
Induced drag is one third of parasite drag, so CD = (4/3) CD,0
Induced drag is zero because the wing is at minimum drag
questions.explanation: Setting dTR/dV = 0 yields CL = √(CD,0/K), so K CL2 = CD,0 and parasite drag equals induced drag. Three times parasite drag is the minimum-power condition; one third of parasite drag is the jet best-range condition; induced drag can only be zero when lift is zero.

questions.question: An aircraft with a parabolic drag polar has a minimum-thrust speed VTR,min = 100 m/s. What is its minimum-power speed VPR,min at the same weight and altitude?
questions.explanation: Minimum power required occurs at VPR,min = 3−1/4 VTR,min ≈ 0.7598 × 100 = 76.0 m/s. 100 m/s assumes minimum power and minimum thrust occur at the same speed; 131.6 m/s multiplies by 31/4 (which is the jet maximum-range speed); 57.7 m/s divides by √3 instead of 31/4.

questions.question: At the minimum-power speed VPR,min, which ratio of aerodynamic coefficients reaches its maximum?
options: CL3/2 / CD, where induced drag is three times parasite drag
CL / CD, where induced drag equals parasite drag
CL1/2 / CD, where induced drag is one third of parasite drag
CL alone, just above the stall speed
questions.explanation: Power required is proportional to CD/CL3/2, so minimizing PR maximizes CL3/2/CD at CL = √(3CD,0/K), where Di = 3D0. Maximizing CL/CD gives minimum thrust, maximizing CL1/2/CD gives jet best range, and maximizing CL gives the stall speed.

questions.question: You have a plot of power required PR against airspeed V starting from the origin (0, 0). How do you locate the minimum-thrust speed VTR,min on that plot?
options: Find where a straight line from the origin is tangent to the PR curve
Read the airspeed at the lowest point of the PR curve
Find where the slope of the PR curve is steepest
Find where the PR curve crosses the horizontal PA line
questions.explanation: Because TR = PR/V is the slope of a straight line from the origin to a point on the PR curve, the shallowest line from the origin that touches the curve (the tangent from the origin) marks VTR,min. The lowest point of PR gives VPR,min, the steepest slope is at high speed where parasite power grows as V3, and crossing PA gives Vmax.

questions.section: Thrust available, power available, and maximum speed
questions.question: A twin-engine propeller aircraft has sea-level shaft power P0 = 500 kW per engine, propeller efficiency η = 0.80, and lapse exponent mad = 1.0. What is its total power available at full throttle where ρ/ρ0 = 0.50?
options: 400 kW
200 kW
500 kW
800 kW
questions.explanation: With n = 2 and δt = 1, PA = n η P0 (ρ/ρ0)mad = 2 × 0.80 × 500 × 0.50 = 400 kW. 200 kW counts only one engine; 500 kW omits the propeller efficiency η; 800 kW omits the altitude density factor.

questions.question: An aircraft climbs at constant weight from sea level to an altitude where the air density is one quarter of sea-level density (ρ = ρ0/4). How do TR,min and VTR,min change?
options: TR,min stays the same and VTR,min doubles
Both TR,min and VTR,min double
TR,min drops to one quarter and VTR,min doubles
TR,min stays the same and VTR,min drops to half
questions.explanation: Minimum thrust required TR,min = mg/(L/D)max does not depend on air density, so it stays unchanged. Minimum-thrust speed scales as 1/√ρ, so cutting density by 4 multiplies VTR,min by √4 = 2.

questions.question: For the same climb at constant weight to an altitude where ρ = ρ0/4, how does the minimum power required PR,min change?
options: It doubles, because PR,min scales as ρ−1/2
It stays the same, just like TR,min
It drops to half, because air resistance is lower in thin air
It increases by a factor of four
questions.explanation: Because PR = TR V, keeping the same thrust at twice the true airspeed doubles the power required: PR,min ∝ 1/√ρ, so √4 = 2. Minimum thrust stays constant, not minimum power; thinner air requires a faster true airspeed to hold lift, which raises PR,min.
